stage: second invocation of the multi-command chain, in the same directory family as the first, at its second command
expected: each invocation starts from a clean directory: its first command writes a configuration file into the invocation's own working directory, which the second command then opens by relative path
observed: the first invocation succeeded end to end. In the second, the first command exited 0 after 2.85 s but printed an error that its generated input files already existed beside the shared input files from the first invocation; it wrote no configuration file. The second command then exited 2 after 0.056 s on stderr 'the file does not exist' for that relative path and wrote no files.
fix: Copy the two input files into each invocation's own working directory before its first command, so generated files never collide; also treat an error line in stdout as failure.
why_previous_fixes_missed: They targeted reading output after a successful run; the first invocation never collided, so the shared-input-directory collision on the second invocation stayed hidden until now.
